title: Requisition to approved PO in under two minutes
description: A site planner raises a replenishment requisition, InLumin runs the policy checks, and procurement approves and raises the purchase order without leaving the workflow. All data is synthetic.

steps.notes: Requisitions list. Data table screen for the M1 capture set.

tooltip.title: Everything open, in one queue
tooltip.body: Six live requisitions, two waiting on this approver. Cycle time and off-contract spend are on the same screen — no separate report. Start a new one here.

steps.notes: Filled form: input values, selected options and checked boxes all survive capture.

tooltip.title: Contract pricing applied as you type
tooltip.body: Each line matches against contract CT-2291, so the rate and the amount are the contracted ones. Off-contract lines are flagged before the requisition is ever submitted.

tooltip.title: Submit for approval
tooltip.body: Routing is derived from cost centre and value — the requester never picks an approver.

steps.notes: Modal screen for the M1 capture set — open dialog state persists in the snapshot.

tooltip.title: Five policy checks, run automatically
tooltip.body: Contract match, budget, supplier qualification, lead time and segregation of duties. The approver sees the one exception rather than re-deriving all five.

tooltip.title: Approve and raise the PO in one action
tooltip.body: Approval and PO creation are the same step, so there is no re-keying between the requisition and the order.

tooltip.title: The audit trail writes itself
tooltip.body: Every check, acknowledgement and approval is on the PO. This is the artefact an auditor asks for, produced as a by-product of the workflow.

endScreen.headline: Requisition to PO in 1.9 days, not 11
endScreen.body: This flow used synthetic data on a demo tenant. The same policy checks run against your contracts, cost centres and delegation limits.
